prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on what you need (individual/ACA plan, Medicare, small‑group/employer plan) and what matters to you (lowest premium, broadest network, in‑person help, fee transparency). I can help you find specific names if you tell me which type of plan and your ZIP code — otherwise here’s a practical way to get the right broker and some resources to find reputable ones in Kansas City.

Quick questions
- Are you shopping individual/marketplace (ACA), Medicare (Part A/B/D/Medigap/Advantage), or employer/small‑group coverage?
- Do you want someone local for face‑to‑face help or is phone/email OK?
- Any priorities (low cost, particular doctors/hospitals, bilingual, evening/weekend availability)?

How to find a good broker in Kansas City
1. Use official and professional directories
   - Healthcare.gov navigator/assister for ACA marketplace help.
   - Medicare.gov or your state SHIP program for unbiased Medicare counseling (Missouri and Kansas SHIP offices).
   - National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) “Find a Broker” tool for credentialed agents.
   - State insurance department “license lookup” (Missouri and Kansas) to verify a broker’s license and any complaints.

2. Look for independence and carrier access
   - Prefer independent agents who are appointed with multiple carriers so they can compare plans across insurers (rather than a captive agent who only offers one company).

3. Check experience and specialty
   - Make sure they have relevant experience: many agents specialize in Medicare, ACA, or employer plans. Ask how many clients they currently serve in your plan category.

4. Read reviews and get references
   - Check Google/Yelp reviews, but also ask the broker for local client references you can call.

5. Ask about costs and conflicts
   - Most brokers are paid by carriers (commissions), but some charge client fees. Ask up front how they are paid and whether they’ll shop multiple carriers.

Interview questions to ask a prospective broker
- Which insurers and plan types do you represent?
- How many clients do you help with (Medicare/ACA/small group) each year?
- How will you compare and present plan options to me?
- Do you charge any client fees? If not, how are you compensated?
- Will you help with enrollment and with claims/renewals after I pick a plan?
- Can you provide references from clients in Kansas City?

Red flags
- Refusal to put answers in writing (fees, services).
- Only offering one carrier with no explanation why.
- Pressure to enroll immediately or claim of “only one left” without documentation.
- Poor reviews about post‑enrollment support (claims help, renewal assistance).

Where I can help
If you tell me your ZIP code and whether you need Medicare, ACA individual/family, or employer coverage, I can pull together a shortlist of well‑reviewed local brokers/agents and draft an email or call script to contact them.
